# Persistence migrations and draft recovery

- Preserve current persistence decisions unless a requirement warrants migration; do not replace a working aggregate model just because the original scaffold used separate tables.
- Make invoice/line updates and number allocation atomic. Enforce ownership, constraints and concurrency in persistent storage, not only UI state.
- Use additive reviewed migrations; do not edit previously applied migrations or reset live data. Back up production data before migration and document rollback.
- Debounce autosave, expose save/offline/failure states and explicit retry. Prevent stale responses and out-of-order writes overwriting newer edits.
- Use version conflict checks and explicit recovery for concurrent devices. Isolate local recovery by user/business and clear private cached data on sign-out.
- Allow incomplete drafts to save while blocking invalid issuance. Duplicating creates a fresh unnumbered draft and appropriate new dates.
- Preserve manual due-date overrides; changing terms only updates dates still controlled by terms.
